system_overview: This specification models a modified Two-Phase Commit protocol with a Backup Transaction Manager (BTM). When the primary transaction manager fails after making a decision, the BTM can take over and finalize the transaction, preventing the blocking problem inherent in standard two-phase commit. The specification is written in PlusCal and translated to TLA+, modeling both resource manager and transaction manager failures.
actors_and_components: The system has three types of processes: (1) A set of resource managers that prepare, commit, abort, or fail. (2) A primary transaction manager that decides to commit or abort the transaction, and may fail after deciding. (3) A backup transaction manager that activates when the primary TM has failed and takes over the decision-making role using the same commit/abort logic.
state_variables: The system tracks: (1) A mapping from each resource manager to its current state, which can be working, prepared, committed, aborted, or failed. (2) The transaction manager's state, which can be initial, commit, abort, or hidden (representing failure after a decision). (3) A program counter for each process tracking its current control location.
initial_state: All resource managers are in the working state. The transaction manager is in its initial state. All process program counters are at their starting labels.
actions: Resource managers loop while working or prepared, and in each iteration nondeterministically choose one of three actions: (1) Prepare: transition from working to prepared. (2) Decide: if the TM has decided to commit, transition to committed; or if still working or the TM has decided to abort, transition to aborted. (3) Fail: if RM failure is enabled and no other RM has already failed, transition to failed. The primary TM nondeterministically chooses to commit or abort: it commits if all RMs are prepared (or any RM is already committed), and aborts if any RM is aborted or failed and no RM has committed. After deciding, if TM failure is enabled, the TM transitions to the hidden state (simulating a crash). The backup TM activates only when the primary TM is in the hidden state: it then makes the same commit or abort decision using identical logic and sets the TM state accordingly.
safety_properties: Type correctness: each RM is always in one of the five valid states and the TM is always in one of the four valid states. Consistency: no two resource managers may be in conflicting final states (one committed and another aborted).
liveness_properties: Termination: all processes eventually reach a terminal state. This is guaranteed by weak fairness on all processes, including the BTM which ensures progress when the primary TM fails.
model_bounds: The set of resource managers is a constant, typically three. Two boolean constants control whether RM failure and TM failure are enabled.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed for all processes (resource managers, primary TM, and backup TM). The model assumes clean crash failures, not Byzantine behavior. The BTM does not fail. At most one RM may fail at a time. The specification uses PlusCal with explicit program counter labels for each step. The commit condition accounts for the case where the primary TM committed and an RM learned the decision before the TM failed, allowing the BTM to also commit. Stuttering is allowed when all processes have terminated to prevent false deadlock detection.
